lines.note: Ge'ez splits the title and the two clauses about the Lord as light, saviour, and defender across two verses.
Ge'ez separates the evildoers approaching to eat his flesh from the enemies weakening and falling.
Ge'ez separates the army and fearless heart from the war and confidence.
Ge'ez separates dwelling in the Lord's house from beholding his beauty and visiting his temple.
The divisions overlap: Ge'ez 10 joins the rock clause ending Greek 5 to the lifted-head clause beginning Greek 6; Ge'ez 9 and 11 complete those Greek verses.
Ge'ez separates the pleas not to turn away in anger from the pleas for help and against abandonment.
